certainty_reasoning: Married, on the same two-source footing as the first marriage: the Complete Letters editors state it ('Married 1899; he succeeded as fifth Baronet in 1907'), and Wikipedia supplies the day, the church and his dates.
date_label: M. 27 July 1899 at St Saviour's, Jersey; ended by her death, 12 February 1929
summary: Two years after divorcing Edward Langtry, Lillie Langtry married Hugo Gerald de Bathe at St Saviour's in Jersey - the island she had come from - with only her daughter and the officials there. He was seventeen years younger. In 1907 he inherited the baronetcy and she became Lady de Bathe; they spent the last years apart, and she died in Monaco in 1929.

sources.quote: However, in 1899, she married 28-year-old Hugo Gerald de Bathe (1871-1940). The wedding between Langtry and de Bathe took place in St Saviour's Church, Jersey, on 27 July 1899
sources.context: Wikipedia, 'Lillie Langtry'. The elision drops the intervening account of his family and prospects; the article adds that her daughter Jeanne Marie was the only other person present apart from the officials.
sources.supports: The second marriage: year, husband's identity and dates, exact date and place.
